title: Threat Research Engineer
description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100\* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

* *Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.*

An overview of this role

As an Threat Research Engineer at GitLab, you'll research emerging security threats and turn your findings into protection for GitLab customers. You'll investigate new attack surfaces, including AI coding agents, agent plugins, and package ecosystems, and build systems that help detect threats and improve vulnerability advisories.  
This is a full-stack role: you'll take an idea from the first research question to a working proof of concept, deploy it, and analyze the results yourself. Artificial intelligence (AI) is central to how we work. You'll use AI tools daily and build agentic workflows for research, analysis, and detection.  
  
What you'll do

* Research new attack surfaces and threat vectors, including AI coding agents, agent plugins, and package ecosystems.
* Find and responsibly disclose vulnerabilities in open source projects and developer tools.
* Analyze software supply chain incidents and events.
* Build AI-powered workflows and agents that automate research, analysis, and detection.
* Build and maintain the cloud-based systems behind our detection and advisory work.
* Improve the quality and coverage of our vulnerability and malware advisories.
* Write up your findings as blog posts and present them at conferences.

What you'll bring

* Hands-on security experience in research, malware analysis, penetration testing, or security tooling, with an understanding of package ecosystems and software supply chain attacks.
* Both a developer mindset and an adversarial mindset: you can build systems and think about how to break them.
* Demonstrated experience using AI in real work, such as building with large language model (LLM) application programming interfaces (APIs) or agent frameworks like LangChain, LangGraph, or agent software development kits (SDKs).
* Strong programming skills in Go or Python, with good software engineering practices, including testing, code review, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), and writing maintainable code.
* Experience deploying and running production services on a public cloud.
* The ability to map attack vectors, explain trade-offs, and use data to move experiments forward, balancing quality, speed, and customer outcomes.
* Clear writing for engineers and a general audience, and keeping up with security and AI industry trends.
* Helpful, but not required: Google Cloud Platform (GCP); Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) entries or published findings; research on AI agents, LLM applications, or Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers; blogs, talks, or open source security tools; Terraform or OpenTofu; databases or data pipelines at scale; reverse engineering.
* You don't need deep knowledge of compilers or static application security testing (SAST) engines. A high-level understanding is enough.

About the team  
We're the Threat Research group. We maintain the GitLab Advisory Database, which powers GitLab's dependency scanning, and publish our findings on the Security Labs blog.  
Our work includes research on the Shai-Hulud npm worm and a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in Serena, a popular MCP coding agent.

* Flexible Paid Time Off
* Team Member Resource Groups
* Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan
* Growth and Development Fund
* Parental Leave

Additionally, studies have shown that people from underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. **Country Hiring Guidelines:** GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. * Developing composite identities that combine machine and human authorization for AI
* Improving service accounts and secure automation

We are looking for a hands\-on Software Engineering Manager to lead the Funded Development (Services / NRR) POD — the cross\-functional team accountable for delivering customer\-funded enhancements and bespoke solutions on top of our trading platform. The role sits at the intersection of engineering delivery and commercial commitment and is measured on how predictably the POD ships committed customer work on time, at the quality bar our clients expect, across multiple concurrent engagements.  

  

This is a working manager role: you are expected to stay close to the code — reviewing designs, code and stepping in on the hardest problems — while primarily driving delivery for the POD. The POD's core surface is Order Routing and the Market Data ecosystem, with regular contributions into Risk, FIX services, trading UI enhancements and other backend systems as customer commitments require.### **Key Responsibilities**

  

* **Delivery \& stakeholder ownership** — Own end\-to\-end delivery of customer\-funded projects across multiple concurrent engagements. Run the daily cadence (standups, sprint reviews, hand\-offs) and act as the primary engineering point of contact for Product and Project Management on requirements, estimation, capacity planning, project tracking, CR workflows, and risk. Surface schedule and scope of risk early with credible mitigations, and provide honest, timely status to Client Services, Sales, Platform, Release Engineering, and senior leadership.
* **Hands\-on technical leadership \& design** — Stay close to one or more components across the TT platform (Order Routing, Market Data, Risk, FIX services, trading UI). Author tech design documents for non\-trivial customer\-funded features and review designs produced by the team — ensuring correctness, performance, blast radius on shared components, rollout / rollback, observability, and long\-term supportability. Set the quality bar through architecture, design, and code reviews in modern C\+\+, and be the escalation\-of\-last\-resort on hard issues.
* **Cross\-component versatility \& engineering excellence** — Deliver across a broad surface — Order Routing, Market Data, Risk, FIX services, and trading UI enhancements — as customer commitments evolve. Drive engineering best practices across the POD: modern C\+\+ standards, multithreading and concurrency correctness, performance tuning, automated testing, and CI hygiene. Treat customer\-funded work as first\-class product code, not throwaway one\-offs, and build a POD that can flex across components without becoming shallow on any of them.
* **AI\-assisted engineering** — Champion the adoption of AI coding assistants and agentic tooling (e.g., Claude Code, Copilot, and internal AI tooling) across the POD to accelerate delivery, code review, test authoring, design exploration, and production diagnostics. Set the bar for responsible use — quality, security, IP protection, and human accountability for shipped code — and share patterns that work back into the wider engineering org.
* **SE \+ SQE leadership** — Lead a cross\-functional POD of Software Engineers and Software Quality Engineers. Foster a shared ownership model where quality is designed in, not bolted on, and where SQEs are equal partners in scoping, automation, and release readiness.
* **People management \& culture** — Line\-manage the POD: 1:1s, feedback, growth plans, hiring, and calibration. Build a fair, sustainable delivery culture that can absorb context switching and shifting priorities without burning people out or letting quality slip.

* Proven track record delivering complex, customer\-committed software projects in an Agile environment — working closely with Product and Project Management on estimation, planning, and CR workflows — and managing multiple concurrent engagements with changing priorities, aggressive timelines, and frequent context switching, while still meeting commitments.
* Hands\-on experience using AI coding assistants and/or agentic developer tooling (e.g., Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, or equivalents) in real delivery — with a clear point of view on where they add leverage, where they don't, and how to keep quality, security, and IP under control.

As a Custom Software Engineer, a typical day involves creating tailored software solutions by designing, coding, and improving various components within systems or applications. Collaboration with different teams and continuous refinement of software elements are integral parts of the daily workflow, fostering innovation and responsiveness to evolving project needs.  

We are looking for a Senior Network \& Kubernetes Migration Specialist (6–9 years experience) to lead and execute large\-scale AWS network and container platform migration initiatives. This role requires deep expertise in AWS networking, enterprise hybrid connectivity, and strong hands\-on experience with Amazon EKS from both infrastructure and application perspectives.  

  

1\. AWS Network Architecture \& Migration  

* Lead end\-to\-end migration of on\-premises and hybrid network environments to AWS.
* Design complex AWS networking architectures including multi\-account VPC strategy, subnet segmentation, routing, NAT, IGW, and load balancing.
* Architect and implement AWS Transit Gateway (hub\-and\-spoke, inter\-region, multi\-account connectivity).
* Design hybrid connectivity using AWS Direct Connect, Site\-to\-Site VPN, and BGP routing.
* Perform network segmentation aligned with zero\-trust principles.
* Lead migration risk assessment, rollback planning, and phased cutover strategies.
* Optimize network cost, latency, and high availability post migration.

  

2\. Security \& Governance  

* Define and enforce enterprise\-grade security policies using Security Groups, NACLs, AWS Network Firewall, and third\-party firewalls.
* Implement inspection VPC and centralized egress architectures.
* Collaborate with security teams on compliance and regulatory requirements.
* Implement guardrails using SCPs and IAM boundaries.

  

3\. Amazon EKS – Infrastructure Perspective  

* Design and operate production\-grade Amazon EKS clusters.

This is not a machine learning or AI research role; the engineer does not train foundation models. It is also distinct from traditional full\-stack engineering, where systems follow deterministic logic rather than selecting execution paths at runtime. Two consequences shape the work. First, the most important logic often lives in natural language: instructions, prompts, tool descriptions, guardrails, escalation rules, all of which must be engineered, versioned, and reviewed with the same discipline as code. Second, because behavior is probabilistic, correctness is established by measuring behavior at scale rather than by asserting fixed outputs, making automated evaluation a first\-class engineering activity rather than a quality\-assurance afterthought.


HR sharpens both points along two independent axes.

**Accuracy.** An agent answering on payroll, benefits, leave, or a lifecycle event touches statutory entitlement, jurisdiction\-specific policy, and an employee's pay. A confidently wrong output is not a bad answer; it is a missed enrollment window or an incorrect leave balance acted on in good faith.

**Audience.** HR data is among the most sensitive on the platform, and correctness of content is not sufficient. An answer grounded in a record or knowledge article the requestor is not entitled to read is a data exposure even when every fact in it is true, and manager\-scope and employee\-scope views of the same question have different correct answers. Access boundaries have to be enforced in the retrieval and tool layer rather than requested of the model.


At IC4 the engineer owns AI design decisions across the domain, not within a single feature, and owns the correctness of what ships whether a person or an agent produced it.


What you do Build AI\-native capability across the employee lifecycle


Design and ship features built around agentic behavior — intent interpretation, multi\-step reasoning, tool invocation, and action on the user's behalf — together with the data models, integrations, and channels that make them usable in production. In HRSD this spans guided service selection and intake, natural\-language case creation and enrichment, conversational case status and in\-flight change, tiered resolution of payroll and benefits inquiries, case triage, routing, and deflection, eligibility and entitlement inquiry, and agent\-driven execution of onboarding, transfer, and offboarding lifecycle events.


Design AI\-driven autonomous workflows


Decompose HR processes into the steps and decision points an agent can execute: determining where autonomy is appropriate, where a checkpoint with a person is required, and how exceptions, retries, and hand\-back are handled. Anything that changes pay, employment status, or a restricted record, and anything touching employee relations or investigation, needs a human decision point by construction. The design must make that distinction structural rather than advisory.


Author and maintain agentic instructions as engineering artifacts


Write, structure, and version the system instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, and escalation paths that govern agent behavior in the domain, under code review, source control, and regression coverage. Own the shared instruction and tool\-description surface that adjacent teams build against. Because HRSD ships as product, customers configure, extend, and override that surface on their own instances: treat it as public API, with upgrade\-safe extension points and versioning discipline to match.


Build automated evaluation and test non\-deterministic behavior


Design and operate the evaluation that makes change safe: golden datasets, multi\-turn conversation suites, model\-as\-judge scoring calibrated to human review, CI gates, and drift detection, plus adversarial, jailbreak, grounding, and tool\-selection testing. Extend that coverage to the HR\-specific failure classes — access\-boundary violations in retrieval and citation, PII leakage across scopes, and jurisdictional and policy\-variant correctness — and keep evaluation meaningful across customer configurations rather than against a single reference dataset. Own the resolution, containment, and quality metrics the domain is measured on, including whether they are instrumented correctly in the first place.


Design conversational experiences across channels


Build experiences that hold context across turns, hand off cleanly between automated and live HR agents, and behave consistently across employee\-facing portals, chat shells, workplace messaging clients, agent workspace, and voice — accounting for what voice imposes: latency budgets, barge\-in, speech recognition error on names and plan terminology, disambiguation, and explicit confirmation before consequential actions.


Specify precisely and direct AI coding agents


Convert requirements into testable specifications with explicit scope, constraints, non\-goals, and acceptance criteria; decompose work into agent\-sized tasks; supervise several workstreams in parallel; and review agent output for correctness, spec adherence, security, and maintainability. You own the result regardless of what produced it.


Own quality, safety, and reliability in production


Monitor conversation quality, containment, hallucination rate, tool\-selection error, and unsafe or unauthorized action. Defend against prompt injection and data leakage across integration surfaces, including the paths where user\-supplied content — case notes, inbound email, attachments, authored knowledge — enters agent context. Maintain reasoning\-trace observability and model rollback mechanisms, and feed production failures back into specifications and evaluation sets. Because HR conversation content is itself restricted, design that observability to be diagnosable without exposing what was said. Lead root\-cause analysis when agentic behavior deviates from intent, and hold the line between a genuine model failure and a platform or configuration failure presenting as one.


Ground it in solid full\-stack delivery


Build the application, APIs, data models, and integrations around these capabilities: front\-end experiences for employees, managers, and HR agents, server\-side logic, and the connections to HCM, payroll, benefits, identity, knowledge, and the adjacent service domains HR cases cross into — with the CI/CD, observability, and upgrade\-safe extensibility expected of production software.


Collaborate across product, design, and engineering


Partner with product managers, designers, conversation designers, HR domain and compliance partners, and engineers to define success criteria and communicate capability and risk clearly. Mentor IC1 to IC3 engineers, and raise the team's practices around instruction authoring, evaluation, and accountable agent use.
